newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: African flights back to normal as strike ends.
newsitem.headline: African flights back to normal as strike ends.

text.p: Most scheduled flights across West Africa were operating normally on Friday after air traffic controllers in the region called off a pay strike that devastated Christmas travel, airline officials said.
Union leaders at the regional Agency for the Safety of Aerial Navigation (ASECNA) declared the stoppage ended on Thursday night, shortly after announcing a 72-hour extension.
A union statement said the move followed a promise by ministers of tourism of the 15 member states of ASECNA to examine their grievances at their meeting next month. "Having
confidence in their goodwill and following consultations, we have decided to suspend the action and return to work immediately," said the statement issued by union president Alexandre Damiba.
Air traffic controllers responsible for flights over 16 million sq km (six million sq miles) of territory launched the strike at dawn on Wednesday to back demands for better pay and conditions.

The action had already eased markedly by Thursday afternoon after controllers at major West African airports, including the regional hub Abidjan, ignored the extension order and returned to their radar screens.
Both multinational airline Air Afrique and Air France, the dominant carriers in the region who suffered most from the strike, said they were back to normal operation.
"The situation is back to normal and all our flights are assured," said Air Afrique spokesman Marc Amoussou, adding that special flights would help clear the backlog of passengers.
Air France said its Abidjan-Paris service on Friday was expected to operate on schedule.
Just about all ASECNA members are former French colonies in West and Central Africa and the Indian Ocean, but the strike also affected non-Francophone neighouring states.
